questions.text: B+ Trees are considered BALANCED because
questions.solution:
In a B+ tree all leaves are always at the same depth (splits and merges happen at the root level), so every root-to-leaf path has the same length.

Answer: the lengths of the paths from the root to all leaf nodes are all equal

options: the lengths of the paths from the root to all leaf nodes are all equal.
the lengths of the paths from the root to all leaf nodes differ from each other by at most 1.
the number of children of any two non-leaf sibling nodes differ by at most 1
the number of records in any two leaf nodes differ by at most 1.

questions.text: Suppose  a database schedule S involves transactions T1,...,Tn. Construct the precedence graph of S with vertices representing the transactions and edges representing the conflicts. If S is serializable, which one of the following orderings of the vertices of the precedence graph is guaranteed to yield a serial schedule?
questions.solution:
Each edge [latex]T_i\rightarrow T_j[/latex] means [latex]T_i[/latex] must come first. A serializable schedule has an acyclic precedence graph, and any topological order respects every edge, so it gives an equivalent serial schedule.

Answer: Topological order

questions.text: In an Ethernet local area network,which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- A station keeps sensing while transmitting (that is how it detects collisions) False
- The jam signal tells everyone a collision happened; padding is something else False
- After a collision the station stops transmitting False
- Exponential backoff makes stations wait random, growing times, so they are less likely to collide again True

Answer: The exponential backoff mechanism reduces the probability of collision on retransmissions

questions.text: Identify the correct sequence in which the following packets are transmitted on the network by a host when a browser requests a webpage from a remote server,assuming that the host has just been restarted.
questions.solution:
After a restart, nothing is cached:
1. DNS query to get the server's IP
2. TCP SYN to open the connection
3. HTTP GET on that connection

Answer: DNS query, TCP SYN, HTTP GET request
